# Pi.js 2.3.0 - Comprehensive Reference for LLMs

## Overview

Pi.js is a browser-only WebGL 2 library for retro-style graphics, bitmap text, sound, and input.
It provides GPU-accelerated, pixel-perfect rendering with no runtime dependencies.

- Official website: https://pijs.org
- Version: 2.3.0
- Primary global: `pi`
- Short alias: `$`, created only when another library has not already defined it
- Coordinates: logical pixels with `(0, 0)` at the top-left
- Rendering: automatic; drawing commands are batched internally

The generated TypeScript declarations in `pi.d.ts` describe the Full bundle's signatures.
Separately loaded plugins supply declarations that augment the API when imported. This file
focuses on API selection, common behavior, and correct usage patterns.

Use the named `$` import for ES modules:

```javascript
import { $ } from "pijs-web";

const screen = $.screen( "320x200" );
screen.print( "Hello, Pi.js!" );
```

ESM also provides default `pi` and named `pi` exports. IIFE bundles expose the globals above.
Examples use `$` as the API binding.

## Calling Conventions

Most commands accept either positional arguments or a single options object:

```javascript
$.line( 0, 0, 100, 100 );
$.line( { "x1": 0, "y1": 0, "x2": 100, "y2": 100 } );
```

Create a screen before using a screen-scoped command. Screen objects expose the same
screen-scoped commands, so code can avoid repeatedly changing the active screen.

## Screens

### Creating Screens

```javascript
const main = $.screen( "320x200" );
const scaled = $.screen( "320m200", "scaled-container" );
const extended = $.screen( {
	"aspect": "320e200",
	"container": document.getElementById( "extended-container" )
} );
```

Aspect separators have these meanings:

- `x`: exact logical dimensions
- `m`: scale to integer multiples of the requested dimensions
- `e`: extend the logical area to fill the container while preserving pixel aspect

The full signature is
`screen( aspect, container, isOffscreen, resizeCallback, parent, noCss )`. Prefer an options object when
creating an offscreen or parented screen.
Offscreen screens require exact `x` dimensions. `noCss: true` leaves canvas layout to host CSS;
see [Screen layout](#screen-layout-and-resource-behavior).

### Managing Screens

```javascript
const first = $.screen( "320x200" );
const second = $.screen( "160x100" );

$.setScreen( first );
const sameScreen = $.getScreen( first.id );
console.log( sameScreen.width(), sameScreen.height(), sameScreen.canvas() );

second.removeScreen();
first.removeScreen();
```

Calling a method on a removed screen throws an error with code `DELETED_METHOD`.

### Parented Offscreen Screens

An offscreen screen can share an existing screen's WebGL context. This makes drawing its
framebuffer into the parent more efficient.
The relationship controls context affinity only; it does not control ownership or cleanup.

```javascript
const main = $.screen( "320x200" );
const layer = $.screen( {
	"aspect": "160x100",
	"isOffscreen": true,
	"parent": main
} );

layer.cls();
layer.circle( 80, 50, 30, "red" );
main.drawImage( layer, 80, 50 );

layer.removeScreen();
main.removeScreen();
```

`parent` is valid only for an offscreen screen and may be a current screen object or screen ID.
Invalid or deleted parents throw `INVALID_SCREEN_PARENT`.

### WebGL Context Recovery

Context loss suspends every screen sharing the WebGL context. Drawing and queued shader passes
are discarded, reads return transparent pixels, and deferred pixel filters are canceled. A read
spanning loss returns transparent pixels even if restoration completes before it settles.

Restoration rebuilds resources for all surviving screens before rendering resumes. Framebuffers
start transparent, so redraw the scene. Settings, views, font selections, shader handles, and
display shader settings remain available. Images and font atlases upload again when needed;
framebuffer pixels and GPU-only glyph edits are lost. A failed rebuild leaves the group suspended
and reports `WEBGL_CONTEXT_RESTORE_FAILED` to the console.

## Drawing and Blending

```javascript
$.screen( "320x200" );
$.setColor( "white" );
$.pset( 10, 10 );
$.line( 10, 20, 100, 20 );
$.rect( 10, 30, 80, 40, "red" );
$.circle( 160, 100, 30, "blue" );
$.ellipse( 240, 100, 30, 15, "green" );
$.arc( 160, 100, 50, 45, 270 );
$.bezier( 10, 180, 80, 100, 240, 100, 310, 180 );
$.paint( 0, 0, "#202040", 0.1 );
```

`rect()`, `circle()`, and `ellipse()` use the current color for the outline and the optional
`fillColor` for the interior. `paint()` also accepts an optional boundary color after tolerance.

`arc()` angles are degrees, clockwise from the positive x-axis. Equal angles draw nothing;
positive or negative differences of at least 360 degrees draw one outline matching `circle()`.
Shorter differences wrap clockwise. Sweeps within 0.0001 radians (about 0.00573 degrees) of a full
turn are treated as complete circles.

Only two blend modes are supported:

```javascript
$.setBlend( "replace" );
$.setBlend( "alpha" );
```

Use `setNoise( noise, seed )` for optional per-channel drawing noise. Use filled primitives to
construct wider or shaped strokes.

### Polygons

Full includes the polygons plugin automatically. With Lite, load the standalone polygons bundle
after Pi.js. Do not load it again with Full: duplicate registration throws `DUPLICATE_PLUGIN`.

`polygon( points, fillColor )` and `polygon( { points, fillColor } )` are screen commands.
Points may be flat coordinate arrays, typed arrays, or arrays of `{ x, y }` objects. Coordinates
are rounded to integers and require at least three distinct points. The path closes implicitly.
The outline uses the current color. An optional fill uses nonzero winding, including for concave,
self-intersecting, and overlapping paths. Null or undefined fill draws only the outline; matching
fill and outline RGBA values skip the outline pass. Filling restores the current drawing color.
The collection identity caches coordinates and lazily generated fill spans. Treat points and
their objects as immutable and replace the outer collection when editing coordinates.

### Clearing and BASIC-Style Drawing

```javascript
$.cls();
$.cls( 20, 20, 80, 40 );
$.pset( 150, 100 );
$.draw( "C2 R15 D15 L30 U15 R15" );
```

`draw()` supports the BASIC-style direction commands `U`, `D`, `L`, `R`, `E`, `F`, `G`, and `H`,
plus move, color, paint, turn, arc, and blind-move commands.

## Colors and Palettes

Colors may be palette indices, CSS color strings, hex strings, RGB/RGBA arrays, or color objects.
Palette index 0 is always transparent black. When setting a palette, supplied colors begin at
index 1.

```javascript
$.screen( "320x200" );
$.setPal( [ "white", "red", "green", "blue" ] );
$.setPalColors( [ 2, 3 ], [ "orange", "lime" ] );

const orangeIndex = $.getPalIndex( "orange", 0 );
const orange = $.getPalColor( orangeIndex );
$.setColor( orange );

const palette = $.getPal();
console.log( palette.length, $.getColor(), $.getColor( true ) );
```

`getPalIndex()` returns the closest index inside the optional `0..1` tolerance or `null` when no
color matches. `addPalColors()` appends colors that do not exist and returns their new indices.
Palette edits affect later drawing and do not recolor framebuffer pixels already drawn.

Defaults apply to screens created afterward:

```javascript
$.setDefaultPal( [ "black", "white", "red", "green", "blue" ] );
$.setDefaultColor( 1 );
const screen = $.screen( "320x200" );
screen.setBgColor( "#101020" );
screen.setContainerBgColor( "black" );
```

### Multiple Settings

`set()` accepts options corresponding to current `setX` commands:

```javascript
$.screen( "320x200" );
$.set( {
	"color": 2,
	"blend": "alpha",
	"font": 1,
	"pos": { "col": 2, "row": 3 },
	"bgColor": "#101020"
} );
```

`set()` validates every option name before applying settings. Unknown names throw `INVALID_OPTION`
and apply nothing; invalid options objects throw `INVALID_OPTIONS`. Null settings are skipped.
Global settings can be set before creating a screen. Screen settings require an active screen,
or a `"screen"` setting earlier in the same options object. `undefined` arguments take defaults.

## Images and Sprites

### Loading

Images and sprites retain their source colors when the screen palette changes.
Use the shader API for recoloring.

```javascript
const imageName = $.loadImage( {
	"src": "player.png",
	"name": "player",
	"onError": function( error ) {
		console.error( error );
	}
} );

const sheetName = $.loadSpritesheet( {
	"src": "sprites.png",
	"name": "player-sheet",
	"width": 32,
	"height": 32,
	"margin": 1
} );

await $.ready();
```

Both loaders return the registered name. `getImage( name )` returns the underlying image or
canvas element; `getSpritesheetData( name )` returns frame metadata. `getImage()` also accepts
direct image sources or a `Screen`: an onscreen screen returns its canvas, and an offscreen
screen returns a canvas copy of its logical pixels.
URL loads hold `ready()` until they settle. Failed resources remain registered; using one throws
`IMAGE_LOAD_FAILED`, while using a still-loading resource throws `IMAGE_NOT_READY`.

### Drawing

```javascript
$.screen( "320x200" );
$.drawImage( imageName, 160, 100, null, 0.5, 0.5, 2, 2, 45 );
$.drawSprite( sheetName, 3, 200, 100, null, 0.5, 0.5, 1, 1, 0 );
```

The transformation order after position is `color`, `anchorX`, `anchorY`, `scaleX`, `scaleY`,
then `angle` in degrees. `blitImage()` and `blitSprite()` are lower-level replace-mode variants;
their angle is in radians.
Image drawing and shader samplers also accept `HTMLImageElement`, `HTMLVideoElement`,
`HTMLCanvasElement`, `ImageBitmap`, `ImageData`, `OffscreenCanvas`, and Pi.js screens directly.
Supply usable pixels for direct sources; they do not hold `ready()`.

### Capturing and Removing

```javascript
const captureName = $.createImageFromScreen( "capture", 0, 0, 63, 63 );
$.drawImage( captureName, 100, 20 );
$.removeImage( captureName );
```

`createImageFromScreen()` uses inclusive corner coordinates `x1`, `y1`, `x2`, `y2` and returns
the stored image name. `removeImage()` completes queued draws before releasing textures from all
screens. A later draw with the removed name throws `IMAGE_NOT_FOUND`. Removing a pending image or
spritesheet cancels it silently, releases its readiness wait, and makes the name reusable at once.

## Pixels

`get()` uses `x`, `y`, `width`, and `height`, returning a two-dimensional `[row][column]` array.
It returns palette indices by default. Use `asIndex: false` for `PiColor` values.

```javascript
$.screen( "320x200" );
$.rect( 10, 10, 40, 30, "red" );
const pixels = $.get( 10, 10, 40, 30 );
$.put( pixels, 70, 10 );

const color = $.getPixel( 10, 10 );
console.log( color.r, color.g, color.b, color.a );
```

`getAsync()` and `getPixelAsync()` provide promise-based reads. Removing the screen rejects
pending reads with `SCREEN_REMOVED`. `put()` accepts palette-index arrays and skips index 0 unless
`include0` is true; color-object arrays cannot be passed to it.

`filterImg( filter, x1, y1, x2, y2 )` defers a CPU filter for an inclusive rectangle. Its callback
receives a reusable `Uint8ClampedArray` containing `[ r, g, b, a ]`, plus view-local `x` and `y`.
Return truthy to keep the modified pixel, or falsy to make it transparent. The region and view are
captured at the call, but pixels are read when the filter runs, including synchronous drawing
after the call. Continue on a later task or animation frame to capture the result or draw above it.
Screen removal or context loss cancels queued filtering.

```javascript
$.filterImg( function( pixel ) {
	pixel[ 0 ] = 255 - pixel[ 0 ];
	pixel[ 1 ] = 255 - pixel[ 1 ];
	pixel[ 2 ] = 255 - pixel[ 2 ];
	return true;
} );
```

## Bitmap Text

Pi.js supports bitmap fonts only. Built-in font IDs are 0 through 4.
Font 1, the default 6x8 font, is ready synchronously; other built-in fonts require `ready()`.
The built-in fonts use IBM PC code page 437 glyphs at codes 0–255, with ASCII at 32–126.
For example, the é glyph is code 130, `String.fromCharCode( 130 )`. Printing counts UTF-16 code
units; an unavailable glyph consumes a cell without drawing. Pending or failed font images also
advance the cursor without drawing and warn once.

```javascript
const fontId = $.loadFont( {
	"src": "font.png",
	"width": 6,
	"height": 8,
	"margin": 0
} );

await $.ready();
$.screen( "320x200" );
$.setFont( fontId );
$.setPrintSize( 2, 2, 1, 1 );
$.setPos( 2, 3 );
$.print( "Bitmap text" );
$.setPosPx( 10, 80 );
$.print( "Centered", false, true );
```

Other text helpers include `getPos()`, `getPosPx()`, `getCols()`, `getRows()`, `calcWidth()`,
`setWordBreak()`, `setChar()`, `getAvailableFonts()`, and the global `setDefaultFont()`.
`loadFont()` accepts URL strings, image elements, canvases, and `OffscreenCanvas`. A synchronous
setup failure registers nothing. A failed URL load remains registered and selectable after its
readiness wait settles. `setChar()` updates the shared font's glyph without modifying its original
source element. `setPrintSize()` scales must be finite and positive; padding must be nonnegative
integers.

## Views

Views provide nested local coordinates and clipping. A child origin is relative to its parent.
`width()` and `height()` return the requested active-view size, not the effective clipped size.
Pushing and popping views saves and restores the parent's print cursor.

```javascript
$.screen( "320x200" );
$.print( "Main" );

$.pushView( 20, 20, 120, 80 );
$.cls();
$.rect( 0, 0, $.width(), $.height(), "#202040" );
$.print( "Panel" );

$.pushView( 8, 16, 80, 40 );
$.print( "Child" );
const screenOrigin = $.viewToScreen( 0, 0 );
const localAgain = $.screenToView( screenOrigin.x, screenOrigin.y );
console.log( localAgain );
$.popView();

$.popView();
$.resetView();
```

`popView()` on an empty stack throws `VIEW_STACK_EMPTY`. `resetView()` discards the entire stack,
returns to full-screen coordinates, and resets the print cursor. Input remains screen-relative;
call `screenToView()` before comparing pointer coordinates with view-local content.

## Shaders

GPU framebuffers, image samplers, and custom shader outputs use **premultiplied RGBA**: RGB
is multiplied by alpha. Keep RGB between zero and alpha, and use zero RGB when alpha is zero.
Multiply all four channels to change opacity. To perform straight-color math, divide RGB by
alpha only when alpha is nonzero, then multiply the resulting RGB by the output alpha.

JavaScript colors, pixel read results, palette matching, filter callbacks, and captured canvas
images use straight RGBA. Readback returns zero RGB for fully transparent pixels; low-alpha
RGB is quantized by the internal RGBA8 storage.

Custom shaders are GLSL ES 3.00 fragment shaders. Pi.js supplies the vertex stage. Every usable
shader must declare `uniform sampler2D u_texture`.

### Framebuffer Passes

`applyShader()` inserts a full-framebuffer pass at the current point in draw order. Drawing after
the call is not processed by that invocation. An active view does not restrict the shader pass.

```javascript
const invert = $.createShader( `#version 300 es
precision mediump float;
in vec2 v_texCoord;
uniform sampler2D u_texture;
out vec4 fragColor;

void main() {
	vec4 color = texture( u_texture, v_texCoord );
	fragColor = vec4( color.a - color.rgb, color.a );
}` );

$.screen( "320x200" );
$.rect( 10, 10, 40, 40, "red" );
$.applyShader( invert );
$.line( 0, 0, 80, 80 );
```

### Display Shaders and Uniforms

Display shaders affect final presentation without changing logical framebuffer pixels. While one
is active, the canvas backing store may follow the CSS output size; logical drawing dimensions
still come from `width()` and `height()` outside a view.

```javascript
const tint = $.createShader( `#version 300 es
precision mediump float;
in vec2 v_texCoord;
uniform sampler2D u_texture;
uniform float u_gain;
out vec4 fragColor;

void main() {
	vec4 color = texture( u_texture, v_texCoord );
	fragColor = vec4( clamp( color.rgb * u_gain, 0.0, color.a ), color.a );
}`, { "u_gain": 1.0 } );

$.screen( "320x200" );
$.setDisplayShader( tint, { "u_gain": 0.8 } );
$.setDisplayShaderUniforms( { "u_gain": 0.6 } );
$.setDisplayShader( null );
```

Pi.js owns built-ins such as `u_texture`, `u_sourceSize`, `u_outputSize`, `u_time`, and `u_frame`.
Custom uniforms support scalars, vectors, matrices, arrays, and image samplers. Values must match
the reflected GLSL type and component count.

### Diagnostics and Cleanup

```javascript
const info = $.getShaderInfo( invert );
console.log( info.compiledScreenCount, info.queuedPassCount );
$.removeShader( invert );
$.removeShader( tint );
```

Shader compilation occurs synchronously on first use per screen. Invalid source, handles, or
known uniform values throw synchronously. `removeShader()` finishes queued passes, clears display
use, deletes cached programs, and invalidates the handle.

## Input

The keyboard, pointer, and gamepad plugins share these rules:

- The first read or handler registration starts tracking. After a stop command, only the matching
  start command resumes.
- A handler is identified by its mode and function (and key, for the keyboard). Registering it
  again does nothing, and `once` removes it before it runs.
- `offX( mode, fn )` removes one handler, `offX( mode )` every handler of the mode, and
  `offX( null, fn )` the function from every mode. `offX()` with neither throws `INVALID_MODE`.
- State is updated before handlers run. A handler added during an event first runs for the next
  one; a handler that throws is reported with `console.error()` and the others still run.
- Releases the player did not make, from a hidden page, a stop command, or a cancelled pointer,
  reach `"up"` handlers with `cancelled: true`; the keyboard also releases on blur.
- Event data is frozen. Invalid arguments throw `TypeError` or `RangeError` with per-parameter
  codes.

### Keyboard

```javascript
const left = $.inKey( "ArrowLeft" );
if( left ) {
	playerX -= 1;
}

function jump( keyData ) {
	console.log( keyData.code, keyData.cancelled );
}

$.onKey( "Space", "down", jump );
$.offKey( "Space", "down", jump );

// A combination runs when every key is held; it receives the keys' data in order
$.onKey( [ "ControlLeft", "KeyS" ], "down", function( keys ) {
	save();
} );
```

Name keys by code (`"KeyA"`, `"Space"`, `"ArrowLeft"`) for game controls, or by value (`"a"`) for
typed characters. `inKey()` without a key returns a frozen array of the held keys.
`setActionKeys()` replaces the keys whose browser default is prevented, and `removeActionKeys()`
removes some.

`input()` returns a promise and optionally accepts a callback. It reads its own keys, so they do not
reach `onKey()` or `inKey()`; Escape or `cancelInput()` resolves it with `null`.

```javascript
const name = await $.input( "Name: " );
const age = await $.input( {
	"prompt": "Age: ",
	"isInteger": true,
	"maxLength": 3
} );
```

### Mouse, Touch, Press, Click, and Wheel

These are screen commands on an onscreen screen. Mouse, touch, press, and click data share one
shape: `x`, `y`, `lastX`, `lastY`, `buttons` (1 left, 2 right, 4 middle; 1 while a touch is down),
`action`, `type` (`"mouse"`, `"pen"`, or `"touch"`), `id`, and `cancelled`. The modes are
`"down"`, `"move"`, and `"up"`.

```javascript
$.onMouse( "move", function( mouse ) {
	if( mouse.buttons & 1 ) {
		$.pset( mouse.x, mouse.y );
	}
} );

// Each touch arrives in its own call, in an array of one
$.onTouch( "move", function( touches ) {
	for( const touch of touches ) {
		$.circle( touch.x, touch.y, 3 );
	}
} );

// Press follows the mouse or the primary touch
$.onPress( "down", function( press ) {
	console.log( press.type, press.x, press.y );
} );

// A hit box is { x, y, width, height }; custom data is the second argument
$.onClick( function( click, button ) {
	console.log( "clicked", button );
}, false, { "x": 10, "y": 10, "width": 60, "height": 20 }, "start" );

$.onWheel( function( wheel ) {
	scroll += wheel.deltaY;
} );
```

Use `inMouse()`, `inTouch()`, and `inPress()` for polling; `inMouse()` and `inPress()` return
`null` before the first event. A click needs the same pointer's press and release inside its box;
right and middle buttons do not click. While a screen has wheel handlers, the wheel does not
scroll the page over its canvas. `setPinchZoom()` and `setContextMenu()` are per screen.

### Gamepads

```javascript
$.setGamepadDeadZone( 0.15 );
$.onGamepad( "connect", function( pad ) {
	console.log( "pad", pad.index, pad.id );
} );

function update() {
	const pad = $.inGamepad( 0 );
	if( pad ) {
		if( pad.getButtonJustPressed( "south" ) ) {
			jump();
		}
		playerX += pad.getAxis( "leftX" ) * speed;
	}
	requestAnimationFrame( update );
}
update();

$.vibrateGamepad( 0, 200, 1, 0.5 );
```

`inGamepad()` without an index always returns an array, empty while polling is stopped; with an
index it returns the pad or `null`. Pads are live objects updated in place, and "just pressed"
reports what happened since the previous frame's read. Methods take an index or a standard name:
buttons `south`, `east`, `west`, `north`, `leftShoulder`, `rightShoulder`, `leftTrigger`,
`rightTrigger`, `select`, `start`, `leftStick`, `rightStick`, `dpadUp`, `dpadDown`, `dpadLeft`,
`dpadRight`, `home`; axes `leftX`, `leftY`, `rightX`, `rightY`. A `"connect"` handler also receives
the pads already connected. `vibrateGamepad()` returns `false` where the pad cannot vibrate.

## Sound and Music

Sound needs a page served over HTTP(S), and the browser keeps audio locked until the first user
gesture. Sounds, songs, and audio files share 64 voices and mix on the `"sfx"`, `"music"`, and
`"audio"` buses into the master volume and an output limiter.

```javascript
const beepId = $.sound( {
	"frequency": 440,
	"duration": 0.5,
	"volume": 0.8,
	"oType": "sine",
	"attackTime": 0.05,
	"decayTime": 0.1,
	"sustainLevel": 0.7,
	"releaseTime": 0.2
} );
$.stopSound( beepId );

// Positional: frequency, duration, volume, oType, delay, attackTime, decayTime,
// sustainLevel, releaseTime, pan, frequencyEnd
$.sound( 880, 0.1, 0.5, "square", 0, 0.005, 0.05, 0.5, 0.05, -0.5 );

const trackId = $.play( "T120 O3 L4 C D E F G A B O4 C" );
$.stopPlay( trackId );
$.setVolume( 0.75 );
$.setBusVolume( "music", 0.5 );
```

`oType` is `"triangle"`, `"sine"`, `"square"`, `"sawtooth"`, `"white"`, `"pink"`, or a wave table.
PLAY strings use `MA`, `MD`, `MH`, and `MR` for the envelope, `MS`, `MN`, and `ML` for articulation,
`MP` for pan, `WN` and `WP` for noise, and commas for simultaneous tracks.

Audio files are decoded into memory, or streamed with `stream: true`. `playAudio()` returns an
instance ID:

```javascript
const audioId = $.loadAudio( "effect.mp3", "effect" );
$.loadAudio( "theme.ogg", "theme", true );
await $.ready();

$.playAudio( audioId, 0.8 );
const music = $.playAudio( {
	"audioId": "theme", "volume": 0.6, "loop": true
} );
$.pauseAudio( music );
$.resumeAudio( music );
$.setAudio( music, 0.4, 1.25 );
$.stopAudio( audioId );
$.removeAudio( audioId );
```

`stopAudio()`, `pauseAudio()`, and `resumeAudio()` take an instance ID, an audio ID for every
instance of the file, or nothing for all audio. `playbackRate` is 0.0625–16 for decoded audio and
0.25–4 for streamed audio.

The `sound-advanced` plugin, loaded separately, adds `synth()`, held sounds with `releaseSound()`
and `setSynth()`, `sfx()`, `definePreset()`, `generateSfx()`, `defineInstrument()`,
`setBusEffect()`, `getSoundLevels()`, WAV recording with `startRecording()` and
`saveRecording()`, and `onPlay()` handlers timed to the music.

## Plugins

`registerPlugin()` accepts positional arguments or an options object. The initialization callback
receives a controlled `pluginApi`. Commands registered with parameter names receive a normalized
options object.

```javascript
$.registerPlugin( {
	"name": "stars",
	"version": "1.0.0",
	"description": "Adds a star command",
	"dependencies": [],
	"init": function( pluginApi ) {
		pluginApi.addCommand(
			"star",
			function( screenData, options ) {
				const x = options.x;
				const y = options.y;
				const radius = options.radius;
				for( let i = 0; i < 5; i++ ) {
					const angle = ( i / 5 ) * Math.PI * 2;
					screenData.api.line(
						x,
						y,
						x + Math.cos( angle ) * radius,
						y + Math.sin( angle ) * radius
					);
				}
			},
			true,
			[ "x", "y", "radius" ]
		);
	}
} );

$.screen( "320x200" );
$.star( 160, 100, 40 );
```

The plugin API also supports per-screen data, screen initialization and cleanup hooks, readiness
tracking, dependency registration, event cleanup hooks, access to screen data, and utilities.

- Installation is all or nothing: if `init` or its installation on existing screens throws, the
  plugin leaves nothing behind, `getPlugins()` reports its `state` as `"failed"`, and its name can
  be registered again. Registration methods throw `REGISTRATION_CLOSED` after `init` returns.
- `pluginApi.provideService( service )` publishes an object during `init`, and
  `pluginApi.getService( name )` reads the service of a plugin listed in `dependencies`.
- The Full bundle includes gamepad, keyboard, pointer, polygons, and sound. Their standalone
  scripts are for Lite; loading one after Full throws `DUPLICATE_PLUGIN`.
- `clearEvents()` removes handlers a plugin registered through public commands such as
  `onPress()`, and does not restore them. A plugin that needs input should poll it or register
  its handlers again.

IIFE plugin scripts register themselves after Pi.js loads. ESM plugins export an initializer:

```javascript
import { $ } from "pijs-web";
import * as g_soundAdvanced from "pijs-web/plugins/sound-advanced";

$.registerPlugin( {
	"name": "sound-advanced",
	"dependencies": [ "sound" ],
	"init": g_soundAdvanced.default
} );
```

For Lite, import from `"pijs-web/lite"` and register the `sound` initializer from
`"pijs-web/plugins/sound"` before `sound-advanced`.

## Readiness and Animation

`ready()` supports callbacks and promises and waits for the document plus pending registered
resources.

```javascript
$.loadImage( "player.png", "player" );

$.ready( function() {
	$.screen( "320x200" );
	$.drawImage( "player", 160, 100 );
} );
```

```javascript
await $.ready();
$.screen( "320x200" );

function gameLoop() {
	$.cls();
	updateGame();
	drawGame();
	requestAnimationFrame( gameLoop );
}

gameLoop();
```

## Error and Lifecycle Guidance

- Parameter validation and invalid resource use may throw synchronously; do not assume invalid
  operations fail silently.
- Catch shader creation/use errors when accepting user-authored GLSL.
- Balance `pushView()` with `popView()` or deliberately call `resetView()`.
- Retain and remove image names, shader handles, audio IDs, and screens according to application
  ownership.
- A parented offscreen screen is not removed when its parent is removed.
- Do not use an image name, shader handle, or screen object after removal.

## Screen Layout and Resource Behavior

With `noCss: true` (default false), Pi.js leaves automatic canvas, container, html, and body
styles to host CSS. Supply usable canvas layout. Pi.js appends the canvas and manages its intrinsic
size and WebGL resources. Explicit background commands still apply their requested styles.
The `x` and `m` modes keep their requested logical dimensions; `e` computes its logical extent
from the container. With a display shader, backing size follows the canvas CSS content size before
transforms. Canvas and container changes are observed. Hidden hosts keep their last valid allocation
and recover when visible. Offscreen screens accept `noCss` as a no-op.

Pointer input requires an onscreen target. Creating an offscreen screen makes it active; use
`visible.inMouse()` or `$.setScreen( visible )` to read from the visible screen afterward.

Shader `v_texCoord` uses bottom-left/y-up UVs. Custom `sampler2D` sources have the same
orientation as `u_texture`. Drawing coordinates are top-left/y-down; convert UVs to logical pixels
with `vec2( uv.x, 1.0 - uv.y ) * u_sourceSize`. Direct video sources upload when resolved for
drawing or shader use and a decoded frame is available. First use without a decoded frame throws
`IMAGE_NOT_READY`; subsequent unavailable frames keep the last valid upload. Pi.js creates no
video rendering loop; request drawing or shader presentation as frames change.

Image `onLoad`/`onError` exceptions remain visible and release the resource wait exactly once.
`ready()` waits for resources to settle, including failures; it does not guarantee successful loads.
Failed screen creation rolls back its DOM, observers, commands, and GPU resources.
